23                                             Introduction

24          1.      When someone trades in or returns an Apple device, Apple is supposed to stop

25   charging AppleCare+ subscription fees for that device. That is what the AppleCare+ agreements

26   require and what consumers expect. Having traded in an Apple device, consumers have no need

27   to pay for protection or support on that device. Instead of honoring the agreement and

28
     CLASS ACTION COMPLAINT - 1
  1   consumers’ expectations, Apple kept charging Plaintiff and members of the Class she seeks to
 2   represent for AppleCare+ subscriptions tied to devices Apple knew they no longer owned. In
 3   Plaintiff’s case, Apple kept collecting monthly fees for years after the trade-in, amounting to
 4   hundreds of dollars. At the same time, Apple also charged Plaintiff and members of the Class
 5   new monthly AppleCare+ subscription fees for their new devices.
 6          2.      Apple knows when a device covered by an AppleCare+ contract has been traded
 7   in or returned. Apple ties AppleCare+ to a particular device by serial number, it charges fees by
 8   device, and services are available under the contract only in connection with that device. When
 9   consumers like Plaintiff sign up for a monthly AppleCare+ subscription at purchase, Apple
10   automatically enrolls their specific device in AppleCare+ and begins charging fees as soon as it
11   ships. Apple also tracks trade-ins and returns by serial number. It would be just as easy for Apple
12   to automatically turn off AppleCare+ fees when a consumer trades in or returns a device as it is
13   for Apple to automatically start the fees on purchase. But it would be far less profitable.
14          3.      It is wrong for Apple to charge consumers for AppleCare+ tied to devices that
15   Apple knows they no longer own. Apple’s own trade-in terms require consumers to relinquish
16   ownership of the covered devices forever. AppleCare+ is an extended warranty and service
17   contract that is worthless to the consumer without the covered device. Charging for AppleCare+
18   after a trade-in is pure profit for Apple because it cannot incur any replacement, repair, or
19   support-related costs for a device that is out of circulation. For Apple, it’s money for nothing.
20   For consumers, it’s one more obstacle to making ends meet. For both sides, these charges add up.
21          4.      As set out below, Apple breached its contracts with consumers, violated
22   applicable consumer protection laws, and unjustly enriched itself at its customers’ expense. On
23   behalf of herself and the Class, Plaintiff seeks to recover all damages caused by Apple’s
24   wrongful conduct, injunctive relief requiring Apple to stop charging consumers for AppleCare+
25   on devices that have been traded in or returned, punitive damages, and attorneys’ fees.
26
